verdict.rationale: Langfuse documents version control and labels for prompts, which are the centrally managed logic its LLM pipelines fetch at runtime. Review of new versions is supported through experiments, side-by-side comparison, and CI/CD regression gates. Rollback is only implied through labels, and versioning is scoped to prompts rather than broader automations such as evaluator rules or alerts; one user also found the prompt versioning 'pretty behind' PromptLayer on easy rollback. missing for 10: explicit documented rollback workflow, versioning of non-prompt automations (evaluator rules, alerts, workflows), approval-style review of changes, independent hands-on corroboration of rollback.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can version, review, and roll back my automations

citations.quote: Use version control and labels to manage deployments across environments
Run [Experiments](/docs/evaluation/features/prompt-experiments) against datasets to test new prompt versions directly within Langfuse
Compare experiment runs to decide whether a prompt, model, retrieval, or code change is ready to ship.
Use Langfuse experiments in your CI/CD pipeline to catch quality regressions before they ship.
The prompt versioning has been immensely valuable!
